articles.headline: Check Point flags Management Server zero‑day (CVE‑2026‑93616) being used in ransomware attacks
articles.dek: A path‑traversal bug in Check Point's Security Management Server is live in the wild; the vendor supplies a temporary fix and urges immediate remediation.

body.text: Key Takeaway

Check Point disclosed that CVE‑2026‑93616 – a path‑traversal flaw in its Security Management Server – is currently exploited by the Qilin ransomware affiliate, and a temporary mitigation is already available [FACT:99431bdcf9a090652859dbe7194685ba][FACT:c958834f9578dc5007ab20a7d430b86f][FACT:eec6296288d963c69d88d07beb33573c].
Why This Matters

The Management Server holds the central policy repository and credential vault for your firewalls; a successful traversal can let an attacker read or overwrite those files, potentially exposing AI model data, cloud API keys, or routing rules [FACT:d24785f416556e589e51a14390694c08][FACT:fb41b7c700389b4daadcae5e45fe3af9].
What Happened

Check Point observed active exploitation where the Qilin ransomware affiliate abused the path‑traversal to pull authentication tokens from the server and then used those tokens to spread inside target environments [FACT:fb41b7c700389b4daadcae5e45fe3af9][FACT:c958834f9578dc5007ab20a7d430b86f].
Builder View

If you run Check Point Management Server to drive AI/ML workloads or to enforce network policy in the cloud, apply the hotfix now, scan logs for unexpected file accesses, and isolate the server behind a zero‑trust segment. Check Point already shared a temporary mitigation and is working with a handful of affected customers [FACT:eec6296288d963c69d88d07beb33573c][FACT:db5f82224b7229f5405c661843742de9].
Open Questions

What changes will the forthcoming permanent patch introduce to the API surface? How many on‑prem vs. cloud‑native deployments are truly vulnerable? Are there concrete Indicators of Compromise (IOCs) we can extract from the few customers already hit? Check Point has been warning customers for months, and CISA flagged a related issue two years ago, suggesting a lingering attack surface [FACT:4b96282b81c686f1849317fe1fab659e][FACT:f071bbc69aa5769429f5c68fe199c756].
Ardur Take

Treat this as an urgent remediation priority. The advisory comes directly from Check Point, a trusted vendor, but it is currently a single‑source report, so patch now, enforce defense‑in‑depth, and watch for updates on a permanent fix [FACT:99431bdcf9a090652859dbe7194685ba][FACT:eec6296288d963c69d88d07beb33573c].

keyPoints: CVE‑2026‑93616 path‑traversal in Check Point Security Management Server is actively exploited.
Qilin ransomware affiliate uses the bug to harvest authentication data.
Check Point provides a temporary mitigation and is urging immediate patching.
articles.whyItMatters: Compromise of the Management Server gives attackers control over firewall policies and credentials, which can cascade into AI model leaks, cloud resource hijacking, and broader ransomware impact.
articles.readerAction: Download and apply Check Point’s temporary fix today, audit server logs for unusual file reads, segment the Management Server from production workloads, and subscribe to vendor alerts for the permanent patch.
